definitions.gloss: beef that has been ground into small pieces; ground/minced beef
definitions.explanation: A standard grocery-store cut of beef that has been mechanically ground. Used in hamburgers, meatballs, meat sauce, tacos, stuffed peppers, and many other home-cooked dishes. Sold in trays, usually labeled with the fat percentage.

examples.japanese: {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧。
{牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炒|いた}めて→炒める：01879_itameru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{玉|たま}→玉：02221_tama⟧ねぎ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}えて→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。

notes:
Composed of {牛|ぎゅう} (cow, beef) + {挽|ひ}き⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧ (ground meat, from the verb ⟦{挽|ひ}く→挽く：12794_hiku⟧ "to grind, mince"). The {挽|ひ} kanji is very often written in hiragana, so both {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく} and {牛|ぎゅう}{挽|ひ}き⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧ are acceptable; supermarket packaging usually uses the hiragana form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炒|いた}める→炒める：01879_itameru⟧: to stir-fry ground beef
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use ground beef (in a recipe)
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}100⟦グラム→グラム：01354_guramu⟧: 100 grams of ground beef
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}→豚ひき肉：23445_butahikiniku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{合|あ}いびき: a mix of ground beef and ground pork

RELATED FOOD TERMS:
- ⟦{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}→豚ひき肉：23445_butahikiniku⟧: ground pork
- ⟦{鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}→鶏ひき肉：23444_torihikiniku⟧: ground chicken
- ⟦{合|あ}いびき{肉|にく}→合いびき肉：22856_aibikiniku⟧: a mixture of ground beef and pork (very common in Japanese home cooking)
- ⟦ハンバーグ→ハンバーグ：01785_hanbaagu⟧: hamburg steak (Japanese-style patty)
- ミートボール: meatball
- ⟦ミートソース→ミートソース：30415_miitosoosu⟧: meat sauce
- ⟦そぼろ→そぼろ：10383_soboro⟧: crumbly seasoned ground meat served over rice
- タコライス: taco rice (Okinawan dish using ground beef)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the most common choice for home cooking is actually ⟦{合|あ}いびき{肉|にく}→合いびき肉：22856_aibikiniku⟧ — a beef-pork mix — which is considered ideal for hamburg steaks and meat sauce. Pure {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく} is more often chosen for Western-style dishes like tacos, chili, and shepherd's pie. Supermarket prices per 100 grams are typically higher for beef than for pork or chicken.
